items.title: H3-Image Day-0 Support: 4K in 0.87s with Vera Rubin
items.summary_1line: H3-Image on Vera Rubin: 0.87-second 4K generation or 6,115 images/hour on four GPUs, with projected API revenue and support across consumer and data-center hardware.
items.editor_note: First Rubin data point: vLLM's day-0 MiniMax H3-Image support, 4K in 0.87s or 6,115 images/hour on four GPUs.

items.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Vera Rubin NVL72: 58x Throughput vs. GB300 NVL72 at 387 tokens/s
items.summary_1line: On one NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack, vLLM serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on SemiAnalysis AgentX at 1.7M tokens/s per GPU at a P90 of 387 tokens/s per user, 58x GB300 NVL72 at the same interactivity.
items.editor_note: Source of the 58x claim: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one NVL72 rack vs GB300 NVL72 at a P90 of 387 tokens/s per user.

items.title: CoreWeave Reports 2.7x Speedup with Vera Rubin Over GB200 on MLPerf DeepSeek-V3 Benchmark
items.summary_1line: CoreWeave Reports 2.7x Speedup with Vera Rubin Over GB200 on MLPerf DeepSeek-V3 Benchmark HPCwire
items.editor_note: First standardized-benchmark figure: CoreWeave's MLPerf DeepSeek-V3 run at 2.7x over GB200, reported by HPCwire.

editorial.tldr: This is a run of separate vendor benchmark posts for NVIDIA's Vera Rubin, not one event. On Nov 12, vLLM published two day-0 serving results, for MiniMax H3-Image and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on a Vera Rubin NVL72 rack.
editorial.whats_new: CoreWeave reports a 2.7x speedup for Vera Rubin over GB200 on the MLPerf DeepSeek-V3 benchmark (via HPCwire), the first Rubin number in this thread on a standardized suite.
editorial.why_it_matters: Rubin speedup claims range from 2.7x on MLPerf to 58x on a vendor agent workload, so the generation-over-generation gain you plan capacity and cost around depends on which baseline and interactivity target you trust.
editorial.take_for_builders: Hold Rubin capacity and cost projections until you rerun your own workload at your target per-user tokens/s; treat 58x as a vendor ceiling and 2.7x on MLPerf as the more conservative planning number.

beats.headline: vLLM posts day-0 Rubin results for two open-weight models
beats.summary: Two blog posts from the vLLM project: image generation on four GPUs and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on a full NVL72 rack, with the headline 58x figure measured against GB300 at matched per-user speed.

beats.headline: CoreWeave's MLPerf run puts Rubin at 2.7x over GB200
beats.summary: A cloud provider's result on a standardized suite, with a far smaller multiplier than the vLLM agent-workload figure.

open_questions: Does MLCommons publish an audited MLPerf result that matches CoreWeave's 2.7x?
Does any third party reproduce vLLM's 58x DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash figure against GB300 NVL72?
When do CoreWeave or other clouds list Vera Rubin instances with public per-hour pricing?
